coachingPoints: Feet before hands — your base decides the shot; the catch is just delivery.
Catch in your pocket, high and tight; long dips give defenders time to close.
Release on the way up, not at the top — catch-and-shoot is a quick, compact motion.
Keep the same mechanics at full speed as in form shooting; never invent a new form for game shots.
Track makes out of 50 from five spots; honest numbers reveal real progress.
commonMistakes: Catching low at the waist and dipping — fix: practice catching at chest height with a partner, no dip allowed.
Landing off-balance from a slow approach — fix: replace the run with the two-foot hop and land square.
Rushing the release and losing form — fix: speed comes from preparation, not from a hurried, broken motion.
Only practicing stationary catches — fix: add movement: sprint, cut, or come off a screen before each rep.
description: Catch, set, and release in one fluid motion — the most efficient shot in basketball and the foundation of spacing.
gameSituations: Spot-up threes in the corner — the classic catch-and-shoot: drive-and-kick creates it, you finish it.
Fast-break kick-outs — the trailer catches on the wing and shoots before the defense recovers.
Coming off down screens — curl or pop to your spot, catch ready, and shoot over the trailing defender.

howTo.detail: Cut hard to your spot or sprint off the screen. A lazy approach means a late, contested shot.
howTo.title: Move with purpose to your spot

howTo.detail: Finish the approach with a two-foot hop, landing balanced with knees bent and shoulders facing the rim.
howTo.title: Hop into a square stance

howTo.detail: Hands at chest height, fingers up — present a clear target. Catch the ball high, in or near your shooting pocket.
howTo.title: Show hands and catch high

howTo.detail: There is no dip, no extra load. The catch flows straight into your shooting motion — one continuous rise.
howTo.title: Flow straight into the shot

howTo.detail: Extend up through the legs, release with the shooting hand, guide hand passive. Hold the follow-through and watch it drop.
howTo.title: Rise, release, and hold

title: Catch & Shoot
whatIsIt: Catch and shoot is the art of receiving a pass and shooting in one continuous motion — no dribble, no hesitation. It is the fastest shot in basketball and the engine of modern spacing: defenses stretch because shooters punish help with instant threes.

What looks simple is actually a chain of details: the cut to get open, the footwork before the catch, the high catch, and the compact release. Elite catch-and-shoot players make it look effortless because they prepared before the ball arrived.
whyItMatters: Analytics are clear: catch-and-shoot threes are among the most efficient shots in basketball. Every offense needs players who can punish a collapsing defense instantly. For young players, it is also the easiest path to real playing time — coaches always find minutes for someone who moves without the ball and makes open shots.
